summary: Yamhill County summit: crow's nest tree (1916), then a wooden tower (1934) cut to 55 ft in 1955; last manned in 1982; gone by 1996.

facts.design: wooden tower with a 7 x 7 foot cab, with a ground house for living quarters (1934)
facts.status_note: Gone by 1996 per firetower.org and firelookout.com; Wikipedia says abandoned in the 1970s

staffing.status: observers on duty in June 1942; last manned fire lookout in Northwest Oregon, closed at the end of the 1982 fire season

events.note: Crow's nest tree platform, the first structure on the site
Wooden tower; the register gives 65 ft, the September 1934 Forest Log item gives 69 ft under construction
Observers on duty at a June 1942 inspection (report dated July 9, 1942); the inspection describes a 75 ft tower
Register: tower cut to 55 ft and a 10 x 10 foot cab added
New cab built at a cost of $1616.70 per Forest Lookouts; the register dates the cab to 1955
Wikipedia says a station on the peak was abandoned in the 1970s; this conflicts with the 1982 closure
Last manned fire lookout in Northwest Oregon, closed at the end of the fire season (1982 annual report, Forest Grove District)
Gone by 1996 per the register and firelookout.com; removal date not given

corrections.why: 21.0 m (69 ft) matches only the 1934 construction report; the register gives 65 ft for the 1934 tower, a 1942 inspection gives 75 ft, and the tower was cut to 55 ft in 1955

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief asks whether a tower, a camp or only a lookout tree stood here. A crow's nest tree platform came first in 1916, and a wooden tower followed in 1934.
Sources give 65 ft (register, firelookout.com) and 69 ft (1934 Forest Log) for the 1934 tower, 75 ft in a 1942 inspection, and 55 ft after 1955 (register).
The register dates the 10 x 10 foot cab to 1955; the Forest Lookouts page dates a new cab to 1956.
The register and firelookout.com say gone by 1996; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1982 as the last manned year; Wikipedia says a station was abandoned in the 1970s.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m of 21.0 m equals the 69-ft 1934 construction figure, so a single height is misleading (see corrections). The 1955 and 1956 cab dates conflict and are unresolved. The Wikipedia abandonment date (1970s) conflicts with the 1982 closure and was not resolved. The seismograph station comes from Wikipedia only and was not checked on the ground. No access information was found, so no access key. Wikipedia's 2009 wind-farm plan was left out as outdated.
